answer: The protocol validates 1,000 unique location proofs by measuring signal transit across a grid acting as a navigational beacon for every agent. An issuer assigns distinct spatial coordinates, and each signed receipt proves the agent reached the site. A verifier acts as a mirror, reproducing the failure by re-running logs to identify any latency ripple. Each agent must carry a data lantern to illuminate the path; any discrepancy triggers a penalty. Honest nodes pay linear travel costs, while 1,000 fakes create a thread of congestion that is physically impossible to hide without detection.
